$comment: Industry and role framing used to give generated labs a concrete scenario. Industry ids match portal/lib/scenarios.json.

manufacturing.audience: plant supervisors, maintenance technicians, and production planners
manufacturing.problem: Line supervisors lose hours every shift chasing maintenance history, standard operating procedures, and parts availability across SharePoint, a CMMS, and a stack of PDF manuals.
manufacturing.outcome: a single agent that answers equipment and procedure questions, looks up work orders, and files a maintenance request without leaving Teams
knowledgeSources: A SharePoint library of standard operating procedures and equipment manuals
A public product safety and compliance site
A Dataverse table of assets, work orders, and downtime events
sampleQuestions: What is the lockout/tagout procedure for line 3?
Show me open work orders for the packaging conveyor.
Why did line 2 stop last night?

retail.audience: store associates, store managers, and contact-center agents
retail.problem: Associates answer the same product, returns, and promotion questions dozens of times a day, and the answers live in three different systems that change weekly.
retail.outcome: a single agent that answers policy and product questions, checks order status, and starts a return with the right approvals
knowledgeSources: A SharePoint site holding returns, pricing, and promotion policies
The public product catalog and support site
A Dataverse table of orders, returns, and store inventory
sampleQuestions: What is our return policy for opened electronics?
Where is order 10428?
Is the spring promotion still running this weekend?
retail.kpi: average handle time per customer question

financial-services.audience: relationship managers, client service representatives, and operations analysts
financial-services.problem: Client service reps switch between a policy portal, a case system, and email to answer routine account questions, and every answer must be traceable to an approved source.
financial-services.outcome: a single, auditable agent that answers policy questions with citations, retrieves case status, and escalates to a human with full context
knowledgeSources: A SharePoint library of approved product disclosures and servicing policies
The public regulatory guidance site for your market
A Dataverse table of clients, cases, and service requests
sampleQuestions: What documents do we need to add a beneficiary?
What is the status of case CS-4471?
What are the fees on the premium account tier?

healthcare.audience: care coordinators, front-desk staff, and clinical operations teams
healthcare.problem: Care coordinators spend their day answering scheduling, coverage, and protocol questions that are documented but scattered, and every answer has to stay inside compliance boundaries.
healthcare.outcome: a governed agent that answers protocol and administrative questions with citations, looks up appointment details, and hands off to a human when the question becomes clinical
knowledgeSources: A SharePoint library of administrative protocols and patient intake guides
A public clinical guidance site
A Dataverse table of appointments, referrals, and coverage rules
sampleQuestions: What do patients need to bring to a first appointment?
What is the referral process for cardiology?
When is the next available follow-up slot?
healthcare.kpi: coordinator time spent searching for answers

energy-resources.audience: field technicians, dispatchers, and operations managers
energy-resources.problem: Field technicians need site history, safety procedures, and weather conditions before they roll a truck, and today that means three logins and a phone call to dispatch.
energy-resources.outcome: a mobile-friendly agent that answers site and safety questions, pulls live conditions, and logs a field report
knowledgeSources: A SharePoint library of safety procedures and site records
A public weather or grid-status service
A Dataverse table of sites, outages, and field reports
sampleQuestions: What is the safe approach distance for substation 12?
What is the weather at the Willow Creek site right now?
Show me the last three outages for feeder 8.

education.audience: advisors, registrar staff, and student support teams
education.problem: Advising and registrar teams answer the same enrollment, financial aid, and deadline questions every term, and the authoritative answers live across a handbook, a policy site, and a student system.
education.outcome: an always-on agent that answers policy and deadline questions with citations, looks up course and enrollment details, and routes complex cases to an advisor
knowledgeSources: A SharePoint library holding the student handbook and academic policies
The public course catalog and financial aid site
A Dataverse table of students, enrollments, and advising cases
sampleQuestions: What is the deadline to drop a course without a W?
What are the prerequisites for the data science certificate?
How do I appeal a financial aid decision?

nonprofit.audience: program staff, volunteer coordinators, and development teams
nonprofit.problem: A small team supports volunteers, donors, and program participants at once, and the answers are spread across grant documents, a volunteer handbook, and a donor database.
nonprofit.outcome: a low-cost agent that answers program and donation questions, looks up volunteer shifts, and captures new volunteer sign-ups
knowledgeSources: A SharePoint library of program guides and the volunteer handbook
The public donation and program information site
A Dataverse table of volunteers, shifts, and donations
sampleQuestions: How do I sign up for a weekend shift?
Is my donation tax deductible?
What training do new volunteers need?
nonprofit.kpi: staff hours returned to program delivery

executives.emphasis: Executive users want short, decisive answers with the number first and the source second.
executives.designNote: Keep responses to three sentences or fewer and always surface the underlying metric and its date.

sales.emphasis: Sellers want account context and next-best-action, fast, from their phone or Teams.
sales.designNote: Optimize for account lookup, objection handling, and drafting follow-up messages.

marketing.emphasis: Marketers want on-brand copy and campaign facts pulled from approved sources.
marketing.designNote: Constrain tone in the agent instructions and always cite the approved source for any claim.

customer-service.emphasis: Service agents want a correct, citable answer and a clean handoff path when the answer is not enough.
customer-service.designNote: Model the escalation path explicitly and test it as carefully as the happy path.

legal.emphasis: Legal users want traceability far more than they want speed.
legal.designNote: Require citations on every generative answer and disable answers from sources outside the approved library.

finance.emphasis: Finance users want the exact figure, its period, and where it came from.
finance.designNote: Prefer structured data lookups over generative summaries for anything numeric.

hr.emphasis: HR users need answers that are consistent, private, and policy-aligned.
hr.designNote: Pay close attention to authentication so answers can be scoped to the signed-in employee.

it.emphasis: IT users want the agent to resolve tickets and to be governable, monitorable, and reversible.
it.designNote: Wire analytics and solution-based deployment early rather than as an afterthought.

communications.emphasis: Communications teams want reusable, on-message content grounded in approved announcements.
communications.designNote: Use prompt tools with fixed formats so output is consistent across authors.

operations.emphasis: Operations users want the agent embedded in the flow of work, not in another browser tab.
operations.designNote: Prioritize the Teams channel and short, mobile-friendly responses.

sustainability.emphasis: Sustainability users need auditable numbers tied to a reporting period and methodology.
sustainability.designNote: Always return the source document and the reporting period alongside any figure.

accessibility.emphasis: Accessibility-focused users need responses that work with screen readers and simple language.
accessibility.designNote: Avoid dense adaptive cards for primary answers and keep plain-text alternatives.
